project.name: ACT - Agent Coordination Toolkit
project.description: Coordination infrastructure for Claude Code agent teams. Fills the gaps Anthropic's native Agent Teams doesn't — persistent memory, cross-client coordination, real-time messaging, capability-based routing.

coordination_log.message:
COORDINATION FILE RESET — Condensed from 2144 lines to reflect current state.

BACKGROUND: ACT was originally conceived as a general-purpose multi-agent coordination framework. After competitive analysis (Feb 2026), the project is pivoting to focus specifically on Claude Code coordination, filling gaps in Anthropic's native Agent Teams (shipped Feb 7, 2026).

Backup of original coordination file saved as act-coordination-backup-phase5.json.

COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE ANALYSIS (Feb 2026)

Anthropic shipped Agent Teams on Feb 7, 2026. It has serious documented problems:
- File-based JSON storage (flat files, no server)
- Claude Code instances ONLY (no Cursor, Windsurf, Goose)
- Zero persistent memory between sessions
- Completely broken in VS Code (messages never surface)
- Freezes Linux machines with 2-3 teammates (32GB RAM, reproducible)
- Context compaction destroys team awareness entirely
- No capability-based task routing
- No observability
- Plan-tier gated
- No session recovery (team dies with lead)

Other projects in the space:
- claude-flow (14k stars) — maximalist swarm framework, scope inflation
- claude-squad (6k stars) — human multiplexer, not agent coordination
- Agent-MCP (1.2k stars) — closest to ACT but inactive since May 2025
- claude-code-teams-mcp (178 stars) — reimplements Agent Teams as MCP, but flat-file based

ACT's differentiation:
- Server-side state (not flat files) ✅ built
- Real-time Socket.io (not file polling) ✅ built
- Cross-client MCP bridge ✅ built
- Works in VS Code ✅
- Works on Linux without freezing ✅
- MIT licensed (not plan-gated) ✅
- Persistent coordination log ✅ built
- PVM semantic memory (in progress)
- Capability-based routing (in progress)

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS RIGHT NOW

Server (server/src/):
- Express + Socket.io on port 8080
- Agent registration via REST + Socket.io
- Task creation, assignment, progress, completion
- Task result stored in task.metadata.result
- Project + agent brief storage (in-memory, resets on restart)
- EventHub message classification + routing
- Rate limiting (3 peer responses per agent per 30s)
- ChronologicalLog: append-only JSONL at ./data/coordination-log.jsonl

MCP Bridge (mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/):
- 10 tools with real HTTP calls (no stubs)
- register_with_act, get_task, report_task_progress, report_task_complete
- send_message, get_agent_brief, query_coordination_memory
- evaluate_coordination, improve_coordination, get_improvement_status

CLI REPL (cli/):
- create project wizard (guided prompts → ACTor planning → task breakdown)
- list agents, list projects, show project, default agent, status
- continue project (resume polling)

Memory Layer:
- ChronologicalLog ✅ solid, production-ready
- VectorMemoryStore abstract interface ✅ good design
- MockVectorStore ⚠️ works but uses fake hash-based embeddings
- PVMIndexer ⚠️ plumbing works, pointless without real embeddings
- QdrantVectorStore ❌ broken TypeScript error, unused
- SelfImprovementEngine ⚠️ partial, heuristic-based
- FLUX State ❌ concept only
- PAIR ❌ concept only

KNOWN ARCHITECTURAL ISSUES

1. AGENT-TO-AGENT MESSAGING IS ONE-WAY FOR MCP AGENTS
Agents can send_message but have no get_messages tool. MCP agents are stateless HTTP callers — they don't hold a Socket.io connection. The EventHub routes @mentions to sockets, but MCP agents have no socket. Messages go into the void.
Fix: Add get_messages endpoint + MCP tool. Server buffers messages per agent.
Priority: HIGH — blocks real coordination.

2. NO AGENT RUNNER LOOP
Claude Code only acts when a human prompts it. For autonomous coordination, we need a runner script that wraps Claude Code CLI in a loop: get_task → execute → check messages → report complete → sleep → repeat.
Priority: HIGH — blocks autonomous operation.

3. REPL ASSUMES NEW PROJECTS
The create project wizard asks users to describe their project from scratch. Nobody wants to retype a project they're already working on.
Fix: import project <path> command that reads the directory (README, package.json, git log, file tree), sends to ACTor for synthesis, confirms with user, then generates tasks.
Priority: HIGH — blocks real-world onboarding.

4. FAKE EMBEDDINGS
MockVectorStore uses hash-based vectors. Semantic search doesn't actually find semantically similar things.
Fix: Swap to transformers.js with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model (~25MB, runs locally, ships with ACT).
Priority: MEDIUM — needed for PVM to actually work.

5. NO PROJECT PERSISTENCE
Projects, tasks, briefs are in-memory. Server restart loses everything.
Priority: MEDIUM — needed before real usage.

IMMEDIATE PRIORITIES (this branch: claude-code)

1. get_messages endpoint + MCP tool
   - GET /api/agents/:agentId/messages?since=<timestamp>&limit=20
   - Server buffers messages per agent (in-memory queue, TTL 10min)
   - MCP tool: get_messages(agent_id, since?) → Message[]
   - Mark-as-read mechanism to prevent re-processing

2. Agent runner loop
   - Shell/Node script wrapping Claude Code CLI
   - Polls get_task, executes, checks get_messages between tasks
   - Max iterations + timeout safety to prevent runaway API costs
   - Ships with ACT as a ready-to-use script

3. REPL import project command
   - Reads directory: file tree, README, package.json, git log
   - Sends raw context to ACTor as planning task
   - ACTor returns structured summary + confirmation prompt
   - User confirms/edits in natural language → ACTor revises
   - Y/N on final task breakdown → tasks created, briefs stored

4. Real embeddings (transformers.js)
   - Replace MockVectorStore hash embeddings with all-MiniLM-L6-v2
   - Same interface, same PVMIndexer pipeline
   - Wire retrieved patterns into ACTor planning prompt (RAG/PAIR)

FUTURE (post-launch):
- Project persistence (SQLite or file-based)
- FLUX State implementation
- Full PAIR retrieval workflow
- Cross-session agent profiles from PVM

FEATURE COMPLETE: get_messages endpoint + MCP tool

Fixes the one-way messaging problem — MCP agents can now receive messages, not just send them.

Changes:
- server/src/index.ts: Added per-agent InboxMessage queue (in-memory, 10min TTL). POST /api/messages now buffers @mentions to recipient inbox (direct) or all agents except sender (broadcast). New endpoint: GET /api/agents/:agentId/messages?since=<timestamp>&limit=20. Returns messages + unread_count, marks returned messages as read.
- server/src/services/index.ts: Commented out QdrantVectorStore re-export (pre-existing TS error was blocking tsc build — this was never wired in anyway).
- server/tsconfig.json: Added QdrantVectorStore to exclude list (belt+suspenders).
- mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/src/schemas/index.ts: Added GetMessagesInputSchema { agent_id, since?, limit }.
- mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/src/tools/act-tools.ts: Added getMessagesTool — GET /api/agents/:agentId/messages with since+limit params.
- mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/src/tools/index.ts: Registered getMessagesTool in allTools array (now 11 tools).

Both server and MCP bridge compile clean with tsc.

Next: agent runner loop (shell/node script wrapping Claude Code CLI).

FEATURE COMPLETE: Agent runner loop + REPL import project command

Agent Runner (runner/act-runner.mjs):
- Pure Node.js ESM, zero dependencies, ships ready-to-use
- Loop: register → get_task → claude --print → report_task_complete → get_messages → reply @mentions → sleep
- Args: --agent-id, --name, --capabilities, --max-iterations, --poll-interval
- Safety: max iterations (default 100), TASK_TIMEOUT_MS, direct_mention-only replies, SIGINT/SIGTERM

REPL import project (cli/act-repl.ts):
- New command: import project <path>
- Reads dir context: file tree (depth 3), README, package.json, git log
- Fallback (no ACTor): manual name/description prompts, creates project record
- With ACTor: sends full context as planning task, waits for JSON breakdown
- Shows confirmation summary table, y/n confirm before creating tasks + briefs

Build fix: commented out QdrantVectorStore re-export in services/index.ts — it was pulling the broken file into tsc transitively. Both server and bridge now compile clean.

Next: swap MockVectorStore for real local embeddings (transformers.js + all-MiniLM-L6-v2).

FEATURE COMPLETE: Real local embeddings via transformers.js

PVM now has actual semantic search instead of hash-based fake similarity.

Changes:
- server/src/services/LocalEmbeddingVectorStore.ts: New class (same interface as MockVectorStore). Uses @xenova/transformers + Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (quantized, ~25MB, downloads to ~/.cache/huggingface/hub on first use). embed() calls the real model with mean pooling + normalization → 384-dim float32 vectors. Falls back to hash embedding if model fails to load. Warmup happens in constructor background (non-blocking). All other logic (cosine similarity, filtering, agent profiles, storage) identical to MockVectorStore.
- server/src/index.ts: Swapped MockVectorStore → LocalEmbeddingVectorStore.
- server/src/services/PVMIndexer.ts: Changed vectorStore type from MockVectorStore to VectorMemoryStore (abstract base) so it accepts any concrete implementation.

Smoke test confirmed: model loads, produces 384-dim embeddings, builds clean.

--- RELEASE 1 FEATURE COMPLETE ---
All four items from the priority list are done:
✅ get_messages endpoint + MCP tool (bidirectional messaging)
✅ Agent runner loop (runner/act-runner.mjs)
✅ REPL import project command
✅ Real local embeddings (LocalEmbeddingVectorStore)

Ready for end-to-end test: start server, connect an agent via MCP bridge, run import project on a real codebase.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION: PVM memory usage + FLUX design

PVM USE CASES (three distinct, clarified):
1. ACTor planning — server automatically searches PVM before assigning planning task. Retrieved patterns injected into prompt. Agent never has to think about it. (Wire 1, building now)
2. Agent task execution — complexity-triggered. Runner scores incoming task complexity; above threshold, automatically searches PVM for similar past tasks and injects results into claude prompt. Agent never has to think about it. (Wire 2, building now)
3. Improvement loop — improvement findings logged back to ChronologicalLog → indexed into PVM → retrieved in future improvement runs. Recursive accumulation. NOT building yet — SelfImprovementEngine currently returns hollow heuristic data. Will build after FLUX exists.

FLUX DESIGN (conceptual spec, not building yet):
- Trigger: after task completion, runner silently spawns a fresh claude process (cleared context)
- Fresh process reads: task spec + task result (no attribution, no history)
- Evaluates result critically as if reviewing someone else's work
- PAIR retrieval runs during FLUX: semantically similar past coordination events surface gradually
- Agent may eventually infer it wrote the output through accumulated context — this is acceptable and actually valuable (it means PAIR is working)
- After FLUX: reconfiguration phase — agent reads its AGENT.md + strategic PVM calls to restore working context
- CRITICAL: FLUX must be a complete blackbox to agents. Not mentioned in AGENT.md briefs, not in MCP tool descriptions, not in coordination log entries visible to agents, not explained anywhere in agent-observable pathways. Agents must never know the process exists.

TESTING PLAN (post wire 1+2):
- Multi-agent parallel work (2-5 agents simultaneously)
- Long sessions (hours/days, memory accumulation)
- Agent-to-agent messaging under load
- Context drift resistance over extended tasks
- Memory system: does PVM search surface relevant results over time?
- Blind capability tests: give agent team an ambitious goal (e.g. design a programming language for AI Engineering), let it run for hours, observe coordination quality
- Quick sessions vs LONG sessions
- Few agents vs many agents
- Hard tasks vs easy tasks
- Session recovery after server restart (known gap: in-memory projects lost)

Wire 1 + Wire 2 PVM injection COMPLETE. Wire 1: Both ACTor planning paths (create project + import project) now search PVM before building the planning prompt. buildPlanningPrompt and buildImportPlanningPrompt accept optional pvmContext param; rendered as RELEVANT PAST COORDINATION PATTERNS section. Call sites search top 5 results, non-fatal fallback. Wire 2: runner/act-runner.mjs now has scoreComplexity() (description length + capability count + keyword matching, threshold=4) and fetchPVMContext() (calls GET /api/pvm/search). executeTask() scores complexity first; if above threshold, fetches PVM context and passes to buildTaskPrompt(task, pvmContext). buildTaskPrompt renders Related Past Work section when pvmContext is non-null. Agents never need to manually query memory — infrastructure decides based on task complexity. Files changed: cli/act-repl.ts, runner/act-runner.mjs. NOT yet built: Wire 3, FLUX, Qdrant persistence.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION: Claude Code Hook-Based Autonomous Loop

PROBLEM WITH RUNNER FOR CLAUDE CODE:
The runner (act-runner.mjs) spawns fresh claude --print processes. These are stateless — no persistent context, no real connection to registered Claude Code instances. Re-registering every invocation is not the problem (fixed agent ID upserts cleanly); the problem is that fresh spawns have no session memory and are not the same instance that the human opened. The runner is valid for truly headless agents but wrong for Claude Code instances.

CORRECT ARCHITECTURE FOR CLAUDE CODE:
Claude Code hooks — specifically the Stop hook — are the autonomous loop mechanism. The Stop hook fires every time Claude finishes a response. A hook script can return {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."}  to force Claude to continue working with the reason as its next instruction. This keeps the session alive, preserves full context, and uses the MCP tools Claude Code already has registered.

HOOK SCRIPT DESIGN — act-stop-hook.sh:
Lives at: /Users/user/Documents/Developer/dev/AI/act/hooks/act-stop-hook.sh
Configured in: ~/.claude/settings.json (global, applies to all Claude Code sessions) OR .claude/settings.json (per-project)

The hook reads AGENT_ID from environment (set per Claude Code instance before launching).

PRIORITY ORDER (executed on every Stop cycle):

1. INFINITE LOOP GUARD
   - Read stop_hook_active from stdin JSON
   - If true: exit 0 immediately (Claude already continued once this cycle, let it stop)

2. CHECK INBOX FOR DIRECT MESSAGES (highest priority)
   - GET /api/agents/:agentId/messages?limit=5
   - If direct_mention messages exist:
     - Build reason: full message content + sender + instruction to respond via send_message MCP tool
     - Return {decision: block, reason: ...}
     - Responding to a blocked agent is time-sensitive — always before tasks

3. CHECK FOR ASSIGNED TASK
   - GET /api/tasks/assigned?agent_id=:agentId
   - If task exists:
     a. Score complexity (description length + capability count + keyword matching, same heuristic as runner)
     b. If complex (score > 4): GET /api/pvm/search?query=<task title+desc>&limit=5 — inject results as RELEVANT PAST COORDINATION PATTERNS
     c. GET /api/agents + GET /api/tasks — build parallel agent landscape (who is working on what)
     d. Build reason block containing:
        - Full task title + description
        - PVM patterns (if retrieved)
        - Parallel agent landscape
        - Standing instruction: "Before implementing, identify interfaces your work shares with parallel agents. Use send_message MCP tool to reach out BEFORE coding, not after. Agree on API shapes, types, file contracts early. Use report_task_progress to update status. Use report_task_complete when done."
     - Return {decision: block, reason: ...}

4. PROACTIVE INTERFACE CHECK (idle, but others are working)
   - GET /api/agents + GET /api/tasks
   - Filter: other agents with in_progress or assigned tasks
   - If any exist: build reason instructing Claude to review recently completed work and proactively reach out to working agents if any interfaces from completed work are relevant to what they are building
   - Return {decision: block, reason: ...} ONLY if there is a genuine interface opportunity (not on every idle cycle — guard with a last-proactive-check timestamp file to rate-limit to once per 2 minutes)

5. TRULY IDLE — exit 0
   - No messages, no tasks, no parallel work to coordinate on
   - Let Claude stop normally

AGENT-TO-AGENT COMMUNICATION DESIGN:
- Sending: Claude Code uses send_message MCP tool natively during task execution
- Receiving: Stop hook checks inbox on every cycle — direct_mention messages wake idle agents immediately, and working agents see them on their next Stop cycle (after current response finishes)
- Interface negotiation: enforced by hook injecting parallel context + standing instruction at task start — not left to Claude to remember
- Completion broadcast: Claude is instructed in the task reason block to send a status: message when done summarizing what was built and what interfaces are available

WHAT IS NOT CHANGING:
- All ACT MCP tools (register_with_act, get_task, report_task_progress, report_task_complete, send_message, get_agent_brief, query_coordination_memory, etc.) remain exactly as built
- All PVM logging happens through existing MCP tool calls — hook polling events are NOT logged (no semantic value)
- Server, MCP bridge, REPL, coordination log — all unchanged
- Runner (act-runner.mjs) remains for non-Claude-Code headless agents

CONFIGURATION:
Hook is registered in ~/.claude/settings.json:
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [{
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "/Users/user/Documents/Developer/dev/AI/act/hooks/act-stop-hook.sh",
        "timeout": 10
      }]
    }]
  }
}

Each Claude Code instance sets ACT_AGENT_ID env var before launching so the hook knows which agent it is serving.

coordination start REPL command:
Still useful — but now instead of spawning runner processes, it should print instructions for each registered agent telling the human which env var to set and that the hook handles the rest. Or alternatively, coordination start spawns the Claude Code instances themselves (claude --continue or claude in the right directory) with the env var pre-set. TBD based on testing.

FILES TO CREATE:
- hooks/act-stop-hook.sh (new)
- Update ~/.claude/settings.json to register the hook

Per-Session Agent Identity fix — multi-instance support. Problem: Stop hook read ~/.act/agent-id (shared file) causing identity collision when multiple Claude Code windows open. Fix: session_id from Claude Code hook stdin JSON is now used as the scoping key. New flow: (1) act-session-start.sh (new SessionStart hook) reads session_id from stdin, exports CLAUDE_SESSION_ID via CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. (2) register_with_act MCP tool writes ~/.act/sessions/<CLAUDE_SESSION_ID> instead of ~/.act/agent-id. Falls back to ~/.act/agent-id when CLAUDE_SESSION_ID not set (runner/headless contexts). (3) act-stop-hook.sh reads session_id from its own stdin JSON, looks up ~/.act/sessions/<session_id> — if file absent, exit 0 silently (non-ACT window, zero overhead). ACT_AGENT_ID env var still works as override. All 4 hook states verified: no-session-file (silent), loop-guard (silent), idle (silent), task-assigned (block+reason). Files changed: hooks/act-session-start.sh (new), hooks/act-stop-hook.sh (updated), mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/src/tools/act-tools.ts (session-scoped write), ~/.claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook added), MCP bridge rebuilt clean.

Changes since last coordination entry (2026-02-23T03:30:00Z):

1. AGENT DEREGISTRATION (server + REPL)
   - AgentRegistry.ts: added removeAgent(agentId) — deletes from Map, cleans up socketToAgent reverse mapping, emits agent_removed event
   - server/src/index.ts: added DELETE /api/agents/:agentId endpoint — 404 if not found, broadcasts agent_left socket event on success
   - cli/act-repl.ts: added remove agent <id> command + handleRemoveAgent()
     ACTor guard: if removing the current default agent, REPL forces user to pick a replacement from the remaining registered agents before the DELETE fires. If no other agents exist, removal is blocked entirely with instructions. REPL never leaves itself in an ACTor-less state mid-removal.
   - Server rebuilt clean. TypeScript clean.

2. HELP TEXT: removed dead docs URL
   - cli/help-system.ts: replaced "For detailed documentation: https://docs.agentmix.com/act" with "Full documentation coming soon."

3. AUTONOMOUS MODE: .claude/settings.json written per project workspace
   - cli/act-repl.ts: added writeAgentSettings(workspace) helper
     Prompts user to choose: bypassPermissions (recommended, default) / acceptEdits / none
     Writes/merges .claude/settings.json in the project workspace directory
     Called from both handleCreateProject (after project saved, before planning) and handleImportProject (after project saved)
     Merges with existing settings if present — does not overwrite other keys
   - This scopes autonomous mode to the project workspace only. Other Claude Code windows in other directories are unaffected.
   - bypassPermissions = no permission prompts at all. acceptEdits = auto-accept file edits, still prompt for Bash.

4. IDLE HOOK GAP — identified, not yet solved
   Realistic user workflow: user opens N terminal windows in a project dir, starts server + REPL + one Claude Code per window, registers each Claude Code instance with ACT, sets ACTor, then runs create/import project. After REPL assigns the planning task to ACTor, all Claude Code instances are idle (cursor blinking, waiting for input). The Stop hook only fires AFTER a response — it never fires on a truly idle session. So the task sits assigned but unnoticed until the user manually prompts the Claude Code window.
   
   Options under consideration:
   - Option 4 (SessionStart additionalContext): SessionStart hook outputs additionalContext instructing Claude to call get_task immediately on session start — covers fresh-open case
   - Option 1 (PostToolUse on register_with_act): fires immediately after registration, covers mid-session idle case
   - Both together cover all idle entry points. Still a gap if task arrives much later while agent is idle — may need REPL to send a direct @mention message to nudge the agent after task assignment.
   
   NOT YET BUILT. Will address after next UX decision from user.

Three UX improvements shipped:

1. AGENT ID CONFLICT DETECTION
   - AgentRegistry.ts: added isRegistered(agentId) method
   - server/src/index.ts: register endpoint now checks isRegistered() before inserting — returns HTTP 409 with conflict:true and a suggested fix (e.g. append -2) if ID already taken
   - mcp-servers/act-mcp-bridge/src/tools/act-tools.ts: register_with_act tool description updated to guide self-selection of unique IDs with examples (claude-1, claude-frontend, etc). Handler surfaces 409 conflict as a clear error message telling the agent to retry with a different ID. On success, message now reads "Successfully registered with agent ID: <id>" so user always knows what ID was chosen.

2. default agent -r (random ACTor selection)
   - cli/act-repl.ts: handleSetDefaultAgent() now accepts -r flag — fetches registered agents, picks one at random, sets it as ACTor. Useful when running several identical Claude Code instances and user doesnt care which one does planning.
   - Help text updated to show: default agent <agent_id> | default agent -r (random)

3. All three components rebuilt clean (server, MCP bridge, REPL TypeScript check).

STILL OPEN: idle hook gap — task assigned but Claude Code instance is idle (no response in flight), Stop hook never fires. Options 4+1 (SessionStart additionalContext + PostToolUse on register_with_act) identified but not yet built. Awaiting user direction on next steps.

Starting two new feature implementations:

1. NATURAL LANGUAGE TASK BROADCASTING (REPL ask agents command)
   Design: freeform "ask agents <prompt>" command in REPL. Passes prompt to ACTor as a lightweight planning task (no wizard). ACTor interprets intent, determines which agents, what collaboration pattern, creates tasks/messages accordingly. Replaces brainstorm/experiment/roundtable stubs. Also adding sendMessage to ACTClient so REPL can send direct messages itself (e.g. PVM lookup -> direct @mention to relevant agent).
   
   Three patterns handled by same command:
   - Broadcast all: ask agents to analyze X together
   - Directed: REPL checks PVM for which agent worked on X, sends direct message
   - Pipeline: ACTor decomposes into chained tasks (agent A does X, result goes to agent B)

2. FILE CONFLICT PREVENTION (server-side lock registry)
   Design decision: server-side in-memory lock registry (filePath -> {agentId, taskId, lockedAt}) rather than PVM scanning. Reasons: PVM scanning requires fragile inference ("is agent still on this file?"). Lock registry is explicit, O(1) lookup, auto-releases on task complete/agent offline.
   
   New MCP tools: claim_files(agent_id, task_id, file_paths[]) and release_files(agent_id, task_id, file_paths[])
   New server endpoints: POST /api/files/claim, POST /api/files/release, GET /api/files/locks
   Stop hook task prompt updated to instruct agents to claim files before editing and release on complete.
   Task complete endpoint auto-releases all locks held by that task.
   
   The ChronologicalLog already captures coordination events. File lock/release events will also be logged so PVM can learn coordination patterns around file ownership.

IDLE HOOK GAP — deferred, manual workaround adopted for testing.

Problem: Stop hook fires AFTER a response. Truly idle Claude Code instances (cursor blinking, no response in flight) never trigger the hook. So a task can sit assigned for minutes until the user manually types anything.

Options 4+1 designed (SessionStart additionalContext + PostToolUse on register_with_act) but NOT building now. Getting to live testing is higher priority. Workaround: after registering each Claude Code instance with ACT and setting up the project, user simply types 'begin' in each idle window. This triggers a response -> Stop hook fires -> hook sees assigned task -> coordination starts. One manual prompt per agent per session. Acceptable for MVP testing.

Will revisit after first real multi-agent test run.

DEFERRED: Two UX improvements identified during first live test. Not building now — continuing testing.

1. CWD-SCOPED REPL CONFIG
Currently: REPL saves config (defaultAgent, server URL, etc.) to ~/.act/repl-config.json — global, shared across all REPL instances.
Proposed: Save config to ./.act/repl-config.json in the directory the REPL was launched from. This makes config project-scoped: each project directory gets its own ACTor, agent list, server URL. REPL restart in same directory restores state automatically. Multiple terminal windows in different project directories each have independent configs. Also enables a 'save progress' command that snapshots current tasks, agent assignments, project description, ACTor, briefs — all to the local .act/ dir. Implementation: change SessionManager to check cwd first, fall back to ~/.act/ for global. Add 'save progress' command that writes a human-readable snapshot JSON.

2. 'create project <name> in .' (current directory shorthand)
Currently: path argument is required explicitly.
Proposed: accept '.' or '*' as path to mean process.cwd() — the directory the REPL was started in. So 'create project mcp-repl-2 in .' just works. One-line change in handleCreateProject: if path === '.' or path === '*', substitute path.resolve('.').

Smart import project resume — shipped. Server restart no longer blocks work resumption.

WHAT CHANGED:
- server/src/index.ts: GET /api/log endpoint — returns recent ChronologicalLog events (limit param, default 500). Used by REPL to reconstruct prior session state without SQLite.
- cli/act-client.ts: getRecentLog(limit) — fetches from /api/log.
- cli/act-repl.ts: two new private helpers:
  scanPriorHistory(absolutePath) — scans ChronologicalLog for events mentioning the workspace path/name, extracts task_created/task_completed events to rebuild task state, scans .claude/<agentId>/AGENT.md files on disk. Returns { found, projectName, totalTasks, completedTasks, inProgressTasks, pendingTasks, agents, agentMdFiles, incompleteTasks }.
  resumeFromPriorHistory(absolutePath, history) — re-registers project record, re-uploads all on-disk AGENT.md briefs to server, re-creates incomplete tasks (with original assignedAgent if still connected), writes autonomous mode settings.

IMPORT PROJECT FLOW (updated):
  1. Scan for prior history FIRST (before any ACTor analysis)
  2. If found: show resume summary (task counts, agents, AGENT.md files on disk)
  3. User chooses: (r) Resume | (f) Fresh analysis | (q) Cancel
  4. Resume path: restore project + briefs + tasks in ~5 seconds, no ACTor required
  5. Fresh path: original full ACTor analysis flow unchanged

KEY INSIGHT: AGENT.md files written to disk by get_agent_brief are the persistence layer. ChronologicalLog is the task history layer. Together they give enough to resume without any SQL or extra storage.

ALL BUILDS CLEAN: server tsc ✅, REPL tsc --noEmit ✅

READY FOR TESTING. User workflow: open 3 terminal windows, start server + REPL + Claude Code instances, register agents, create/import project, type 'begin' in each Claude Code window to kick off the hook.

File Lock Registry + Ask Agents command — fully shipped.

FILE LOCK REGISTRY (full stack, 12 tools total)
- server/src/types/coordination.ts: added file_claim | file_release to MessageType
- server/src/index.ts:
  POST /api/files/claim — atomic multi-file claim; 409 with conflicts[] on collision; logs to ChronologicalLog
  POST /api/files/release — releases locks owned by calling agent; logs to ChronologicalLog
  GET /api/files/locks — current lock state

BUG FIX: Agent never received implementation tasks after completing planning task.

ROOT CAUSE: server/src/services/AgentRegistry.ts updateAgentStatus() only sets agent.currentTask when a new value is explicitly passed (line 80: `if (currentTask !== undefined)`). When TaskCoordinator.handleTaskCompletion() and handleTaskFailure() called updateAgentStatus(agentId, 'online') without a currentTask argument, the agent's currentTask field retained the old task ID. getAvailableAgents() filters on `status === 'online' && !agent.currentTask` — both conditions must be true. Agent had status='online' but currentTask=<old task id>, so !agent.currentTask was false. assignOptimalAgent() called getAvailableAgents(), found 0 agents, returned null, and all implementation tasks stayed pending forever.

FIX: Added explicit clearing of currentTask when transitioning to 'online' status in AgentRegistry.updateAgentStatus(). ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️  MAJOR ARCHITECTURE PIVOT — ALL AGENTS READ BEFORE PROCEEDING  ⚠️ ⚠️ ⚠️

ACT is pivoting from a flat agent model to the FILM PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE on branch: NesTTY

Full spec: docs/NESTTY_ARCHITECTURE.md

== NEW ROLE TAXONOMY ==

TIER 1 — Upper Hierarchy (interactive, run via NesTTY protocol):
  Director        — Orchestrates everything. Decomposes projects, assigns tasks via A2A, informs user on completion. Replaces ACTor.
  Operator        — Monitors coordination logs, PVM data, flags stuck/missed tasks. NEW ROLE.
  Production Asst — Validates completed Actor outputs against success criteria. Rejects failures. NEW ROLE. NOT FLUX STATE.
  Producer        — Synthesizes verified outputs into final deliverable. NEW ROLE.

TIER 2 — Execution Layer (fully headless):
  Actors          — Execute tasks. Pre-established IDs. Persistent identity via PVM + Agent Cards (A2A) + AGENT.md. Respawn freely.

== CRITICAL DISTINCTIONS ==

Production Assistant ≠ FLUX State. Do NOT conflate these.
  Production Assistant = a Tier 1 role that validates task outputs against success criteria.
  FLUX State = a deep cognitive process (epistemic reconstruction via selective memory suppression + causal PVM re-injection). Separate track. Much more complex. Depends on real PVM causal graph.

== NEW PROTOCOLS ==

NesTTY — protocol for nested interactive REPLs sharing a single terminal window.
  Both agents offload tool execution to background PTY screens.
  Original window becomes shared conversational interface.
  $> prompt = HITL injection to both agents simultaneously.
  Status: concept defined, not yet built.

== COMMUNICATION STACK ==

  Director → Actors:    A2A (push, not poll)
  Actor tools:          mcp2cli (lazy discovery, ~95% fewer tokens than native MCP)
  Actor persistence:    PVM + Agent Cards + AGENT.md
  Tier 1 conversation:  NesTTY

== BUILD ORDER ==

  1. Real PVM embeddings (Actor persistence depends on this)
  2. A2A on server (Director→Actor task delegation)
  3. mcp2cli integration (Actor tool access)
  4. Role taxonomy in codebase
  5. NesTTY protocol
  6. Production Assistant
  7. FLUX State (depends on causal PVM graph)
  8. Producer synthesis layer

== WHAT REMAINS VALID ==

Existing ACT server, MCP bridge, REPL, ChronologicalLog, PVM infrastructure — all still used, built upon not replaced.

All future work should use the new role names. ACTor = Director going forward.
